newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: NAMIBIA'S FISHING INDUSTRY SEEN IMPROVING.
newsitem.headline: NAMIBIA'S FISHING INDUSTRY SEEN IMPROVING.

text.p: Namibia's fishing industry is steering out of choppy waters amid an improvement in maritime conditions, higher quotas and a greater cooperation with the government, an industry analyst said on Friday.

Wilfried Moroff of stockbroking firm Simpson McKie said the Southern African country had seen a vast improvement in the quality of fish and higher yields for fish oil and fish meal due to better oxygen levels and nutritional contents of the waters off its coast in the past five months.

"This...is evident from the unexpected allocation of a 25,000 tonne pilchard quota and the raising of the horse mackerel quota from 250,000 to 350,000," Moroff said in a research report on Namibia's fishing industry.
Moroff said improved fishing conditions off Namibia's coastal waters could boost the country's fishing stocks, such as Namibian Sea Products Ltd and Namibian Fishing Industries Ltd .
He said good spawning of pilchard and horse mackerel had been recorded and hake sizes had also improved since the beginning of the year.

There had also been positive steps towards greater cooperation between the fisheries ministry and the fishing industry, Moroff said. He added bi-annual research trips to determine total allowable catches for various species were now jointly being conducted with vessels manned by both industry and research personnel.
"This will lead to better management of the resource and greater consensus in the allocation of quotas," he told Reuters.
